title: Simultaneous finite-stage lifting of distinguished triangles and finite equations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the pair category $\mathcal P_T$ and finite-stage categories $\mathcal C_E(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], the shift of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], and the distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Equip each $\mathcal C_E(T)$ with the triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] in which [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] chooses its cone triangles, namely the scalar-localization structure of [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] (a triangle is distinguished when it is isomorphic to the image of a distinguished triangle of the integral category $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ whose raw scalar localization is $\mathcal C_E(T)$ by [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]), and the transition functors with their exact structures and coherent comparisons $\sigma$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Give finitely many objects $X=(E_X,K_X)$ of $\mathcal P_T$, finitely many arrows between these objects and specified occurrences of their shifts $[1]$, and finitely many true equations formed from these arrows by composition, identities, zero, addition, negatives, and finitely many applications of $[1]$. Select finitely many triangle rows among this data, each distinguished in $\mathcal P_T$; triangles and their isomorphisms mean [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]. A vertex occurring more than once is a single specified object. Fix also a finite intermediate field $M_0$ of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$.

Then there is a finite field $M\supseteq M_0,E_X$ for every specified $X$, and representatives of all the arrows over $M$, such that all the specified equations hold in $\mathcal C_M(T)$, and all the selected triangle rows are distinguished in $\mathcal C_M(T)$. The lift of $X$ is $X_M=T_{M/E_X}K_X$, shared across all its occurrences; the lift of $X[1]$ is identified with $X_M[1]$ by $\sigma_{M/E_X,K_X}$. In particular a row $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow iZ\xrightarrow pX[1]$ lifts to
$$X_M\xrightarrow{f_M}Y_M\xrightarrow{i_M}Z_M\xrightarrow{\sigma_{M/E_X,K_X}\circ p_M}X_M[1],$$
where $p_M$ denotes its representative with target $T_{M/E_X}(K_X[1])$. A shifted arrow is the shift of its lifted arrow under these identifications. For repeated shifts use the iterated $\sigma$ comparisons. The common-stage images recover the specified arrows and triangle rows through the vertex isomorphisms $X\xrightarrow{\sim}(M,X_M)$ represented over $M$ by $\operatorname{id}_{X_M}$.

proof.text: Choose representatives of the finitely many original arrows and an upper bound L of their stages, every original vertex stage and M0. At a fixed stage, structural induction on Expr proves that its evaluation represents the original term. Identities, composition and addition use the normalized pair-category formulas; negatives follow from the additive inverse equation. The shift case is the defining sigma-conjugated mapAt formula of pbcStageShift. A second induction proves that evaluation commutes with transport: for shift this is Morphism.tr_mapAt, and for the other constructors it is functoriality and additivity.

proof.text: For each asserted equation, the preceding representation calculation and the given equation identify its two mkHom classes at L. The eventual-equality criterion gives a later field at which their transports agree. Bound the finitely many witnesses together with L by Q. The transport cocycle and expression-transport induction give all equations at Q, and preserve them at every later field. Option-indexed upper bounds retain the starting field when a family is empty.

proof.text: Prove the elementary descent of a single isomorphism between stage images. Represent an inverse, impose its two inverse equations after further refinements, and obtain an isomorphism after transport. Apply this to the three components of a triangle isomorphism. Represent the components simultaneously and impose their three commuting squares after a common refinement. The third square uses naturality of the shift comparison. The resulting three component isomorphisms define a stage triangle isomorphism; the associator CommShift equation identifies iterated triangle images with the image of the composite transition.

proof.text: An image of a stage triangle which is common-stage distinguished has a distinguished stage witness by definition. Move the given triangle and witness to a common field, descend their image isomorphism by the preceding step, and apply exactness of transitions and finite-stage isomorphism closure. This makes the given triangle distinguished after some refinement. For the actual rational categories use the already proved qbarScalarExtensionExact infrastructure attached to thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms; its pair-category Verdier conclusion is not used.

proof.text: For each selected row, construct the canonical image recovery triangle isomorphism from its three isoToStage vertex maps. The first two squares follow from mkHom_eq_isoToStage. For the third, exact transition-identification coherence says that isoToStage on the shifted vertex followed by the image of sigma is the shifted isoToStage. Hence its image is common-stage distinguished. Apply the previous refinement lemma to every row and bound their finitely many witness fields. The corrected transported row is isomorphic to its exact scalar extension: the components are inverse associators, with the third square given by pbcStageShift_coherence. Thus every selected row is distinguished at one final field M.

proof.text: Transport the original arrow representatives to M. The two expression inductions recover all terms and preserve the equations already imposed at Q. Reapply mkHom_eq_isoToStage to obtain the required recovery equation for every expression. The canonical recovery triangle isomorphisms from the preceding step have literally the prescribed three vertex components, giving the final conjunct. Vertex objects are always the raw extensions of iterShift at their original field; no fresh object choices or pair-category Verdier axiom enter the proof.
